answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated way, the protocol detects their shared behavior and applies pairwise penalties, so aggregate slashing grows as O(k²), rather than merely with the number of identities. Escrowed collateral makes this loss enforceable; asymmetric depreciation compounds the damage across a coordinated swarm, creating an exponential multiplier in capital lost upon detection. A timber-backed sparrow cannot hide its links by nesting across a reef of aliases.
